source_text:
ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ προσωποποιηθέντα ῥήματα οὔτε τῷ θεσπεσίῳ Παύλῳ ἁρμόζει, οὔτε μὴν παντὶ τῷ συνταφέντι Χριστῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, διότι τῆς ὀνομαζομένης σαρκὸς ἠλευθερώθησαν· οὐ γὰρ ἔτι κατακριθήσονται οἱ τοιοῦτοι διὰ τὴν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ παρακοήν, οὐκέτι βασιλεύει αὐτῶν ἡ ἁμαρτία, οὐχ ὁ θάνατος ὁ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας· συνετάφησαν γὰρ τῇ ζωῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τὴν παρακοὴν
ἐξαφανίσαντος, καὶ τῷ ἑκουσίῳ ἑαυτοῦ θανάτῳ τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐπισυμβάντα ἡμῖν θάνατον ἐκκρουσαμένῳ· γέγονε γὰρ ἑκὼν ὑπὸ νόμον τὸν τῆς παρακοῆς, ἵνα ἡμᾶς 1 τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον τὸν τῆς κατακρίσεως ἐξαγοράσῃ. διὰ τοῦτο ἔφη πᾶς λελυτρωμένος· χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί. ὅτι δὲ ταῦθ' οὕτω καλῶς τεθεώρηται, ἐπιφέρει λέγων ὁ θεῖος ἀπόστολος· οὐδὲν ἄρα κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ· ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν με ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου, καὶ τὰ τούτων ἑξῆς. 3 Πειράσω δὴ διὰ βραχέων καὶ εἰς αὐτὰ τὰ ῥήματα τὰ κατὰ προσωποποιΐαν εἰρημένα παρατρεχόντως εἰπεῖν, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησεν με καὶ δι' αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν. Τὸ ἁμαρτίας ὄνομα οὐκ οὐσίαν ὑφεστῶσαν δηλοῖ, ἀλλὰ τρόπον καὶ βίον τοῦ διημαρτηκέναι τινὰ τοῦ κατὰ λόγον καὶ ὀρθῶς ἔχοντος πράγματος· ὥσπερ γὰρ γενικώτατόν ἐστιν ὄνομα ἡ ἁμαρτία, κατὰ πολλῶν καὶ διαφόρων πραγμάτων κατηγορουμένη. πᾶν δὲ ἁμάρτημα οὔτε λόγῳ οὔτε νόμῳ προστακτικῷ γίνεται· εἰ γὰρ κατὰ νόμον καὶ λόγον ἐγίνετο ὀρθόν, οὐκέτι ἂν ἦν ἁμάρτημα ὡρισμένον καὶ τεταγμένον ἔχον τὸν τῆς γενέσεως λόγον. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ὁ θεῖος ἀπόστολος οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἁμαρτημάτων, ἀλλ' ἁμαρτίας γενικωτάτης ἐχούσης φρόνημα, ἐχούσης νόμον, δυναμένης σοφίσασθαι, ἀφορμὰς πορίσασθαι πρὸς τὴν τοῦ κακοῦ κατασκευὴν μνημονεύει, οὐκ ἄλλον τινὰ γενικωτάτως ἁμαρτίαν ὀνομάζει, ἀλλ' ἢ αὐτὸν τὸν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀρχηγέτην καὶ πατέρα διάβολον. ὅτου χάριν καὶ βασιλεύειν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αὐτὸν ὁ ἀπόστολος ἀπεφήνατο· μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι. ὡς γὰρ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀφ' ἧς ἐπιτηδεύουσι τέχνης καλοῦμεν, οὕτω δὴ καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν διάβολον ὡς πρώτως ἐφευρετὴν γενόμενον τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἁμαρτίαν καλεῖ. Ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν διὰ τῆς δοθείσης τῷ Ἀδὰμ ἐντολῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἠπάτησεν, καὶ δι' αὐτῆς τὸν Ἀδάμ, ἀφορμὰς πορισάμενος διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς. ἔστι δὲ αὕτη· τί ὅτι, φησίν, εἶπεν ὁ θεός· ἀπὸ παντὸς ξύλου τοῦ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ οὐ φάγεσθε βρώσει; καὶ ᾗ δ' ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγησθε ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, διανοιχθήσονται ὑμῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί, καὶ ἔσεσθε ὡς θεοί, γινώσκοντες καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν. σοφίζεται δὲ αὐτοὺς μείζονι ἐπαγγελίᾳ κατακρύψαι τὴν ἀπάτην, ὑπισχνεῖται τὸ πλέον, ἵνα τοὺς τῆς ἐντολῆς φύλακας τῶν τῆς ἀρετῆς βάθρων τῷ ὁμοίῳ αὐτοὺς πτώματι καταστρέψῃ· τὸν γὰρ ἄνθρωπον ἐξοιστρήσας ἴσα θεῷ ἐθέλειν γενέσθαι, τῆς κατ' ἀπάτην ὁμιλίας τὴν ἀφορμὴν ἐπορίζετο ἐκ τῆς παρασχεθείσης ἐντολῆς. ὅτου χάριν ὁ Παῦλος ἔφη· ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με.
thought_title: The substituted persona's words fit neither Paul nor the baptized; 'sin' names the devil
orientation: Didymus is explaining why the words of Romans 7, spoken in a substituted persona, cannot apply to Paul or to any Christian buried with Christ in baptism, and he begins to identify 'sin' as the devil.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore the words spoken in character fit neither the inspired Paul, nor indeed every person buried with Christ through baptism, because they have been freed from the so-called flesh; for such persons will no longer be condemned because of Adam's disobedience, sin no longer reigns over them, nor death which is through sin; for they were buried together with the life of Christ, who through obedience obliterated the disobedience, and by his voluntary death drove out the death that came upon us from it; for he willingly came under the law of disobedience, in order that he might redeem us who are under the law of condemnation. For this reason every redeemed person said: but thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord; for the impossibility of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, God, having sent his own Son in the likeness of flesh of sin, condemned sin in the flesh. And that these things have been rightly viewed in this way, the inspired apostle brings forward, saying: there is therefore no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; for the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and of death, and the things following these. I will attempt then briefly and in passing to speak also to the very words spoken according to speaking in character, beginning from 'but sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.' The name 'sin' does not indicate a subsisting substance, but a manner and way of life of someone having missed the mark of the matter that is according to reason and right; for just as 'sin' is a most general name, predicated of many and different matters. And every sin comes about neither by reason nor by a commanding law; for if it came about according to law and right reason, it would no longer be a sin having a defined and ordered principle of its coming into being. But since the inspired apostle mentions not simply sins, but a most general sin having a mind, having a law, being able to deceive, to procure occasions for the construction of evil, he names no other as sin in the most general sense, but the very originator and father of sins, the devil. For which reason the apostle also declared him to reign over sins: therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body. For just as we call people by the craft they practice, so indeed he calls the devil himself sin, as having become the first inventor of sin. Since therefore through the commandment given to Adam he deceived the human being, and through it Adam, having procured occasions through the commandment. And this is it: why is it, he says, that God said: you shall not eat by eating from every tree in the garden? And on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be as gods, knowing good and evil. And he deceives them by a greater promise to conceal the deception, he promises the more, in order that he may overturn the guardians of the commandment from the pedestals of virtue by a fall like his own; for having goaded the human being to wish to become equal to God, he procured the occasion of the deceptive conversation from the commandment that had been given. For which reason Paul said: but sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'speaking in character' for προσωποποιΐα; this rendering keeps the verbal adjective tied to that term and preserves the rhetorical sense.
rejected: the words spoken in a role

choices.why: The participle ὀνομαζομένης signals that 'flesh' is a name applied to something, not the body itself; 'so-called' preserves Didymus's distancing from the term.

choices.term: τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐπισυμβάντα ἡμῖν θάνατον
choices.english: the death that came upon us from it
choices.why: ἐπισυμβάντα means 'happening upon' or 'befalling'; 'came upon us' keeps the sense of death as an external event resulting from disobedience.
rejected: the death that resulted from it
the death that happened to us from it

choices.english: a most general sin having a mind
choices.why: γενικωτάτης is superlative of 'general' or 'generic'; Didymus contrasts a general category with particular sins, and φρόνημα means 'mind' or 'mindset,' which the devil possesses.
rejected: a most generic sin having a thought
a general sin having an attitude

choices.term: τὸν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀρχηγέτην καὶ πατέρα διάβολον
choices.english: the very originator and father of sins, the devil
choices.why: ἀρχηγέτης means 'originator' or 'founder'; the brief identifies the devil as 'the originator and father of sins,' so this rendering matches the cast description.
rejected: the chief and father of sins, the devil
the author and father of sins, the devil

choices.why: ὁμιλία means 'conversation' or 'speech'; κατ' ἀπάτην modifies it as 'according to deception,' so 'deceptive conversation' captures the devil's reported speech.

pass_b_english: The words spoken in character fit neither the inspired Paul nor anyone buried together with Christ through baptism. Such people have been freed from what is called the flesh. They will no longer be condemned because of Adam's disobedience. Sin no longer reigns over them, nor does the death that comes through sin. They were buried together with the life of Christ, who obliterated disobedience by His obedience and drove out the death that came upon us from it by His voluntary death. For He willingly came under the law of disobedience, so that He might redeem us who were under the law of condemnation. For this reason every redeemed person says: "Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord" (Romans 7:25). For what the law could not do, weakened as it was through the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh; He condemned sin in the flesh (Romans 8:3).

That these things have been rightly observed, the divine apostle confirms when he says: "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death" (Romans 8:1-2), and what follows.

Let me now attempt to speak briefly, in passing, about the very words spoken in character, beginning from: "Sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me" (Romans 7:11). The name "sin" does not indicate an existing substance, but rather a manner and way of life of someone who has missed the mark of what is reasonable and correct. For "sin" is a most general name, predicated of many different things. Every sin comes about neither by reason nor by a commanding law. For if it came about according to law and right reason, it would no longer be a sin, since it would have a defined and ordered principle of its origin.

But since the divine apostle mentions not simply sins, but a most general sin that has a mind, that has a law, that is able to devise clever schemes and procure opportunities for the construction of evil, he names no other as sin in the most general sense than the very originator and father of sins, the devil. For this reason the apostle also declared that sin must not reign in your mortal body (Romans 6:12). For just as we call people by the craft they practice, so also he calls the devil himself "sin," since he was the first inventor of sin.

So then, through the commandment given to Adam the devil deceived the man, and through it he deceived Adam, procuring opportunities through the commandment. The devil says: "Why is it that God said, 'You shall not eat from every tree in the garden'? But on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil." He cleverly devises to conceal the deception with a greater promise. He promises more, so that he might overturn the guardians of the commandment from the foundations of virtue by a fall like his own. For having goaded the man to want to become equal to God, he procured the opportunity for the deceptive conversation from the commandment that had been given. For this reason Paul said: "Sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me" (Romans 7:11).

problems.source_quote: τί ὅτι, φησίν, εἶπεν ὁ θεός· … (quotation of the serpent’s words in Genesis 3:5)
problems.why: The quoted words are from Genesis 3:5 (the serpent), not Genesis 3:1; the citation is incorrect.
problems.ruling: Source quotes only Genesis 3:5 serpent's words; 'τί ὅτι...' is from 3:1 but citation '3:1, 5' misleads.

fixed: The citation was incorrect; the quoted words are from Genesis 3:5, not Genesis 3:1.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'disobedience' for παρακοή, but 'law of disobedience' misrepresents the genitive: Christ came under the law that resulted from disobedience, not a 'law of disobedience'.
problems.ruling: ‘law of disobedience’ misreads genitive; should be ‘law concerning disobedience’, altering meaning

problems.quote: This is what he says: “Why did God say, ‘You shall not eat from every tree in the garden’? And on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil” (Genesis 3:5).

problems.ruling: Greek τί ὅτι, φησίν, εἶπεν ὁ θεός is the devil's words to Eve (Gen 3:1,5), not 'Why did God say'; misattributes speaker and misquotes.

problems.quote: he reigns over sins: “Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body” (Romans 6:12).
problems.source_quote: μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι.
problems.why: Greek says “let sin not reign,” English reverses to “he reigns over sins.”
problems.fix: He declares that sin must not reign in your mortal body (Romans 6:12).

problems.why: The Greek means 'the law of disobedience,' i.e., the law that brings or is disobedience, not 'resulting from.' Christ came under the condemning power associated with disobedience, not a law that disobedience produced.
problems.ruling: Greek τὸν νόμον τῆς παρακοῆς = ‘law of disobedience’, not ‘law resulting from disobedience’

problems.source_quote: τί ὅτι, φησίν, εἶπεν ὁ θεός· ἀπὸ παντὸς ξύλου τοῦ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ οὐ φάγεσθε βρώσει; καὶ ᾗ δ' ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγησθε ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, διανοιχθήσονται ὑμῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί, καὶ ἔσεσθε ὡς θεοί, γινώσκοντες καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν
problems.why: The quoted words are a distorted version of God's command mixed with the serpent's promise. The source does not attribute this to Genesis 3:5; the English adds this citation. The source says 'he says' (the devil speaking), embedding a distorted version. The words combine elements from Genesis 2:16-17 and 3:4-5, but the specific form is the devil's deceptive speech, not a direct scriptural quotation. Adding 'Genesis 3:5' misrepresents the source's presentation.
problems.ruling: English adds citation Genesis 3:5 not present in source; misattributes Scripture

negation: 'μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία' means 'let sin not reign,' not 'he reigns over sins'; corrected.
